The weather? I have no idea. That's the trouble with reviewing a product like this - if it doesn't work, is it the product's fault or is it user error - did I measure something wrong, does it just not work well when it's cold out? Matte liquid lip NOT a gloss. So drying it’s like it pulls every bit of moisture out of your lips! Color - “Stone” I don’t like matte lip products. Usually, they’re way too drying. I don’t mind semi matte lip products that aren’t too dry. But, for the most part, matte lip products just feel too drying on my lips. I was a little confused by the product page for this. The title said it was a “lip liner and lipstick set,” but also said it was a “matte lip gloss” and “liquid lipstick.” I’m not sure how it could be matte and a gloss at the same time. It’s one or the other? So, I looked at the description, whcih said it was a “high pigment lip gloss and lip liner.” It talked about not being sticky, which to me definitely implied a gloss. I’ve never heard a matte liquid lip being described as sticky or non sticky. So, I decided to give it a try. Unfortunately, it’s NOT a lip gloss. This is a matte liquid lip (NOT a gloss) and a lip liner. The lip liner is great. It’s pigmented, creamy and smooth. It glides onto the lips easily. It’s easy to get it where you want it. It lasts well on the lips. It doesn’t feel too dry after applying it, but I did top it with a gloss. The liquid lip on the other hand is horrible! It is waaaaaay too drying! It is NOT a gloss at all! When applying it, it has a grainy, rough feel. Once it drys down, it’s like it sucks every bit of moisture out of your lips. I even tried putting a really moisturizing lip balm on before this and it still seemed to suck out all the moisture leaving cakey, dry looking and feeling lips. It shows every single line, even lines you didn’t even know you had in your lips. It’s crazy! It’s not sticky like it claims, though I don’t know why it would be since it dries down completely matte. I don’t know how well it lasted because I couldn’t stand it on my lips for longer than about 10 minutes and had to take it off. It came off really easy though, so I don’t see it lasting too long. I really hate when product pages are so wrong. This one gave mixed info, not making it clear what it was. I don’t like that at all. It’s like they were trying to make it so people who liked lip glosses would be interested in it, but also make it so people who liked matte lips would be interested in it. You can’t have it both ways. Just describe the product for what it is and let people decide if it’s something for them. Trying to sell it as both is ridiculous! The color “Stone” is pretty. It’s similar to my actual lip color, which is what I prefer. Overall, this isn’t for me. I really liked the lip liner and for the price it isn’t bad just for a lip liner. But, I HATED the matte liquid lip. If you’re someone that likes extremely matte liquid lips, you might like this. But, I honestly don’t know about that. This is the MOST drying matte liquid lip I have ever tried! I give it 2 stars for the lip liner being good and the nice color, but I took off 3 for the horrible description on the product page and the horrible liquid lip.

I am super happy with the purchase overall, and whoever thought this weird looking idea up? GENIUS.

The cute isn't a cover up... A good number of times when you see something as cute as this little bee-esque slicker brush, the manufacturer is covering up a shoddy product and hoping the "awwww, it's SO CUUUUUUTE!!!!!" factor will overwhelm the buyer so much they don't notice and/or care when the product gives up the ghost after only a few uses. So yes, choosing this slicker based on looks probably wasn't the smartest of choices, but in the end it seems to be a good one. This slicker brush is rather nice (and should be for the $20 price tag). It's comfortable to hold. There is weight to it so this doesn't feel flimsy to where the grooming head will break off if you try to comb out a snarl in your pet's fur, or like the body is the thinnest molded plastic they could get away with so it didn't break just removing it from the packaging. Another plus is the end of the tines are tipped/dipped in protective little drops of plastic so the sharp metal ends don't harm your pet. I've always avoided those slickers as they seem like some kind of torture device - how can bare metal ends be comfortable when raked over skin? For taking care of loose hair, this did a bang up job on our two Maine Coons, including the one who absolutely loathes - and I mean to the depths of H.E. double hockey sticks with a side of utter disgust - being brushed. She was adopted from the shelter as an abused kitty from the home of an older cat hoarder, and whatever happened during her first six years of life there were traumatic enough that she will do her best to eviscerate anyone who tries to groom her long fur beyond the area of her neck. She actually lets us very gently use this on the rest of her back and legs and tail for around 45-60 seconds before flipping out, and that's a big improvement! Who knows, maybe she's as amused by the itty bitty bee antenna as we are, but this is the first slicker brush (even with the safety tipped teeth) she's let us use on her back, sides, and legs. The other Maine Coon (a big chonker of a guy) lays on his back with his legs stretched out and purrs like a race car when he gets groomed, so it's not a surprise that he loves this slicker as well. Cleaning the hair out is easy. Just press the button, the plastic disk pushes up, and the hair is forced off of the tines for easy removal. A few of the finer hairs may stick to the plastic or around the tines, but nothing major. When the slicker gets dirty between the base and the underside of the plastic disk, one of those super skinny reusable straw scrubby brushes and a bit of dish soap does the trick. We clip a wooden clothespin on either side of the plastic disk to keep it raised so the tines can air dry and not rust from trapped moisture. Since the tines all seem to be securely anchored to the base of the slicker head, we aren't too concerned about one being pulled out while trying to work through a tangle. It's still a good idea to check the tines every so often to make sure they are all there, none are loose, and that none of the little safety tips at the end of the tines have come off. The only thing that could improve this slicker is a price reduction. A pair of googly eyes wouldn't hurt, either.

This is my first experience using a gel-to-oil cream so I didn't know what to expect, though I hoped it'd leave my skin radiant and glowing (due to the words "GLOW DAY CREAM" in the name). *Note: There's no glow whatsoever. When I dip into a little bit of product, it's a shiny lightweight, non-sticky pink gel. As soon as I apply it to my face or to the top of my hand, it melts, spreads with ease, and leaves my skin velvety soft. The absorption rate is fairly quick compared to similar creams and oils, though usually if something is immediately devoured by my skin, there's no evidence it was there; this, however, leaves my skin smooth and without a greasy residue. It can easily be applied prior to makeup if needed. Finally, this gel has a nice medium fragrance that isn't overpowering or lingering. While I do like the heavy glass jar and think it looks nice, it's quite deceiving. With only one ounce of product inside, I have another jar of face cream that's the same size but contains twice the product. And when compared to other options, ingredients are crucial. (I've included a photo from the box.) While I recognize some as being good organic extracts and oils, the majority sound like chemical compounds I've never heard of. Being a mere breath away from 50, I need to factor in sun damage, a depletion of hormones, thinning skin, melanin spots, and overall aging when I decide what's best for my skincare. This product, while moisturizing, simply doesn't make the cut as something I'll order again. CONS STACKED UP: - Only 1 oz of product - Unfamiliar ingredients - Lacking ingredients I look for based on skincare needs - High price-point PROS: - Leaves skin velvety soft - Nice scent - Absorbs well, no icky residue

It didn’t have any labels on it saying it was cruelty free, but the brand’s website said they’re cruelty free. It also said they use natural and organic ingredients. But, they are not certified organic. It states, “Our products are made with natural and organic ingredients, however, they are not certified organic. All of our products are made in the U.S. using top-quality domesticated and imported ingredients.” I’m not surprised they said they’re not certified organic. I love their honesty. I’ve seen lots of skincare brands claim their products are 100% organic when they definitely aren’t. Most skin care products are water-based and water can NOT be certified as organic, so the possibility of finding a 100% organic skincare product is close to impossible. This claims to be hydrating, brightening, and soothing. It claims to target fine lines around the eyes, reduce appearance of dark circles and puffiness, and hydrate the eye area. It claims the key ingredients are triple peptides, bergamot oil, and citric acid. I included a full ingredient list at the end of my review (marked with 🟣). I included some info on some of the ingredients before that (marked with 🟢). This comes in a nice pump bottle. The pump does squirt out too much if you’re not careful. I find if I carefully press it so I’m not pushing it down all the way, I get enough product and don’t waste any. It’s a thin gel consistency. It glides on nicely. It absorbs quickly leaving my under eyes feeling really hydrated and smooth. I have pretty dry under eyes. If I apply concealer, I have to make sure to moisturize them really well so they don’t look dry and cakey. A lot of the moisturizers that hydrate my under eyes enough are thicker and end up being too heavy to use concealer over. This is PERFECT! It’s thin and lightweight, but feels extremely hydrating! It gives my under eyes enough hydration and plumps them up. It doesn’t leave a sticky residue at all. Concealer goes over it beautifully and looks nice and smooth. I haven’t been using it long enough to say anything about how it works long term on dark circles, firming, etc. But, I can say it’s really hydrating and plumping if you’re looking for something extremely hydrating under the eyes. I’m hopeful for other benefits long term given the ingredients, but even if I don’t get any more benefits, I’m still loving how well it hydrates my under eyes while being so lightweight! Just keep in mind it does have some essential oils and fragrant ingredients in it, so if you have sensitive skin, you might want to avoid this or at least check the ingredient list to see if they’re things that you’re sensitive to. 🟢Info on ingredients Saccharide Isomerate, which is a 100% natural and plant-derived moisturizer. It binds to the skin stronger and longer than other moisturizer ingredients do so it can keep skin hydrated longer than usual. Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1 & Palmitoyl Tetrrapeptide-7 - These are peptides combined to create a compound called Matrixyl 3000. Matrixyl is a highly-effective peptide composition that has been shown to stimulate the production of collagen and elastin, fill in fine lines & wrinkles while restoring elasticity. Sodium Hyaluronate, which is a form of hyaluronic acid (HA). Helps skin hold onto water, making skin more plump and elastic. Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 (aka Argireline), which is called “natures Botox.” It is a synthetic peptide that has several different potential wrinkle-fighting and anti-aging effects. It's so effective, that experts say it's the closest thing to Botox you can get. It prevents the muscle movement that leads to wrinkle formation. Argireline also promotes collagen production and optimizes the function of collagen, which both fight fine lines and improve moisture levels in the skin. The smell is not as strong as other cleaning solutions I have used, but there is a light chemical smell. It comes with a pair of disposable gloves but I did not use them. Since it is a gel it is fairly easy to handle without making a mess. After one hour I wiped it clean with a damp cloth. On the tile it works about the same as soap and water. It still required some scrubbing in certain areas. On the door seal it performed much better. The areas where the gel was applied cleared up not only the mold, but also the soap scum which would not wipe away with just the wet cloth alone. Overall it seems to work fairly well, but it is hard to say how well with no instructions provided. It may take some trial and error to maximize the performance of the gel.

It totally DOES work, but it is totally A PAIN to use. First of all, a lot of people have said this is useless or that it doesn't work. That isn't remotely true. Versions of this device, in one form or another, have been on the market for like 50 years because they DO work. However, the device has an incredibly steep learning curve, is not intuitive to use, has multiple design problems, and costs way more than it should. One of the frustrating aspects of this device is that all of the probes/needles have a spring base. This is there to prevent an inexperienced user (read basically everyone who buys one of these) from accidentally applying current to a part of their skin other than a follicle and thereby potentially causing skin damage. This is an admirable idea, but in practice it means that unless you are 1,000% on-target with the probe, it will just just constantly bounce around on your skin without going into the follicle, truly a frustrating experience! The probes/needles are also far more expensive than professional electrolysis needles, likely due to the silly spring mechanism. I'll note that there are numerous guides for modifying this device (search Inverness OneTouch modifications if curious) to use pro needles which increases its utility and ease of use but also makes it potentially more dangerous if you don't know what you're doing. Now for the good, this device gives you the ability to perform safe, effective, truly permanent hair removal on yourself and/or your loved ones in the comfort of your own home and at your own pace, accounting for your own comfort level. "Professional" electrologists are all over the place in terms of effectiveness, quality, value, actual, literal professionalism, etc. My experience with them has been uniformly poor despite patronizing nearly a dozen at this point. This is cheaper, more convenient, and, assuming you know what you're doing, more likely to be effective on a permanent basis than professional treatment, especially if the electrologist in question is not a 100% galvanic operator (this device is an unsophisticated example of a 100% galvanic machine). Just wish it were a little bit less frustrating to use!

DO NOT use for Sensitive Skin! To start, I "manscape" periodically in the year, and I'm super pale. I have used 'Nair' on my skin before (legs), but I did not suffer chemical burns. Now, the instructions say to leave on no longer than 10 minutes and to test a small area first. I did this. Tested a small area of thick hair not far from the area to be 'scaped'. Oddly enough, around 8 minutes SOME of the hair was wiped off easy enough as I was scared that anything longer would be bad. So after that test patch I decided that the maximum 10 minutes was required for the thick batch of hair below. However I made a grave mistake. I applied a layer near another layer (i did a right half and left half in the same day. For the Love of Soup, do not do this! Wait at least 24 - 48 hours per section, or you will feel the flames of hell on your skin!) Doing the half and half interval of the area caused chemical burns. This was caused from overlapping cream and some areas being on my skin longer than 10 minutes while dealing with the burns of the overlap. The upside of the calming ball lotion, is that it works, but it's the ONLY lotion that eases the pain. I made the mistake of rinsing off the lotion and using skin repair lotion, which intensified EVERYTHING. Another lesson learned- apply the calming lotion after the rinse (and pat dry, don't wipe) and simply leave it. Seek medical attention of skin conditions appear or worsen. Overall, the product did what it was meant to, but my hair was too thick; and my skin was far too sensitive for the chemical composition. And as such, I would recommend trimming first earlier in the day, and apply the 'glaze' to a section (above the pipe and below the pipe) on separate days. DO be careful. I'd recommend Waxing instead.

Interesting idea ... smells great. Cheap packaging. At first, I was a bit skeptical about baby cologne. The act of spraying down your smelly little bundle of joy with cologne seems a bit weird. This does smell pretty darn good! When the bottle arrived, it came capless in an envelope. The bottle feels like very lightweight plastic and cheap. Not sure why they did not go with a thicker plastic or even glass given the price point of this being not exactly on the cheap side. The packaging does not match the price or quality. I wanted the white blossom/citrus version, which was unavailable and worried lavender would be cloyingly sweet and feminine. A few squirts from the bottle and my fears were gone ... this leans more towards feminine but could be worn by a man as well. The note I smell most is orange blossom followed by a faint lavender. It is fresh and captivating and I do get the mediterranean influence ... it smells like Spring on the Amalfi Coast. It's classy and well balanced ... I am a huge fan of colognes/perfumes and have lots of the high end Creed, Aqua di Parma, etc. and while you'll never mistake this for a luxury scent, it's better than a lot of the cheaper colognes and perfumes. I wish I could tell you how babies like it, but mostly my 40 year old girlfriend wears this. It's a splash she puts on after the shower or before heading out when she wants something not as strong or distinctive as perfume. This doesn't last a long time ... maybe an hour or two. Nor does it project incredibly well ... it sits close to the skin. But for the price and how refined it is, it's worth keeping in your overnight bag or gym locker. The ingredients seem to be similar to a normal eau de cologne. I am not sure I'd spritz down an infant with this too often ... but it seems to be a slightly scaled down version of bottled perfume. It still contains alcohol as the first ingredient but feels lighter on the skin. Overall, despite the cheap packaging, this is a nice light scent that is good for adults and probably kids. Orange blossom is one of my favorite smells and it's high on the list of basenotes here. I'd recommend keeping a bottle of this on hand for a quick refreshing spritzdown.
